title: Zucchine Trifolate
subtitle: Italian courgette with garlic, parsley, and olive oil
excerpt: Trifolate means cooked with garlic, oil, and parsley in the style of truffle. The courgette softens and absorbs the flavours from the pan. Simple and good alongside almost anything Italian.
sourceNotes: Classic northern Italian contorno of courgette cooked trifolata-style with garlic and parsley.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best served immediately. The courgette loses texture if kept warm for long.

content.text: Trifolate is one of Italy's simplest cooking methods: garlic, olive oil, and parsley. The courgette needs high heat at the start so it colours rather than steams. Add the parsley at the very end to keep it bright.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over a high heat. Lay the courgette slices in a single layer. Do not move them for 2 minutes.
Flip the rounds and colour the other side for another 2 minutes. Work in batches if needed. Set the coloured courgette aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and chilli flakes to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until pale gold.
Return all the courgette to the pan. Toss to coat in the garlicky oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook for 3 more minutes until the courgette is fully tender. Add a squeeze of lemon if using.
Remove from the heat. Scatter over the parsley. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The courgette is watery and steamed-looking.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough or too many rounds were added at once.
items.fix: Use high heat and cook in batches so the rounds sit in a single layer.

items.cause: It was added when the pan was still on high heat.
items.fix: Reduce the heat before adding garlic and watch it carefully.

items.cause: Under-seasoning or the parsley was added too early.
items.fix: Season generously and add parsley right at the end off the heat.
